options.text: Naming the new vertex $T$ completes the copy.
Any arc centred at $T$ copies $\angle ABC$.
From $B$ and from $T$ draw arcs of the same radius; then transfer the chord between the arc hits on $\angle ABC$ onto the new arc.
The matching arc and chord create $\angle ABC$ at $B$ rather than a copy at $T$.

stem:
Wafa must make an exact copy of $\angle ABC$ at a new vertex $T$ on a fresh ray.

Which construction copies the angle?

teacher.key_rationale: Copying an angle needs the same arc radius at the new vertex and the same chord length between the arm hits transferred onto the new arc. Naming T alone, drawing an unmatched arc, or reversing what the transfer produces all miss that construction.
